text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: cont-batch tail p99 spike detected in us-west-2 (service=runtime-contbatch). p95 increased >3x, p99 ~2.9s, streaming stalls +6% in last 10m. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/p/contbatch/1902

luca: ack — i'm on it, paging SREs. Any immediate customer impact reports?

maya: looking at per-route metrics now. p95 baseline ~110ms -> 420ms. p99 around 2.9s. Streaming stall rate (stream stalls / active streams) jumped from 0.7% -> 6.3%. Affected hostpool: contbatch-gpu-a. Most slow traces are on streaming RPCs that route through cont-batch path.

jordan: fwiw traces show long waits in scheduler loop:
```
scheduler.cpp: enqueue_request() waiting for batch completion (seq_len=10240)
waiting_requests=24, active_batches=2, last_batch_emit_ms=1200
```
Looks like mixed seqlen long requests are blocking smaller ones.

kiara: possible quick mitigation: reduce max_cont_batch_size and enable preemptive_shedding so long seqs don't monopolize a slot. I'll patch runtime flag on contbatch-gpu-a. Command: 
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/v1/runtime/flags -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -d '{"service":"cont_batch","max_batch_size":8,"enable_preemptive_shedding":true}'
```
Do we want to scale pool while we apply?

luca: apply the change to one AZ canary first. kiara, go ahead. i'll monitor.

kiara: applied to contbatch-gpu-a-canary (hosts 3/3). Watching metrics...

incident-bot: config-change recorded: operator=kiara, flagset={max_batch_size:8,enable_preemptive_shedding:true}, target=contbatch-gpu-a-canary

luca: initial signal after canary: p95 dropped to ~180ms, p99 to ~1.1s on canary. Streaming stalls dropped to 2.1% on canary. Good.

maya: good first order improvement. But p99 still above SLO (target p99 < 800ms). We are seeing residual tail from requests that have huge seqlen + KV-cache misses.

jordan: i dug into the KV code — when a long sequence forces an eviction, the subsequent short requests hit a cache recompute path that adds 200-400ms. stack snippet: 
```
kv_cache.cpp: evict_lru() -> async_fetch_model_weights() -> block_on_io()
#012backtrace: evict_lru+0x34, handle_request+0x1a2
```
This couples eviction with scheduler fairness. If we tune batching only, evictions still create microspikes.

kiara: agreed. immediate followups: 1) keep reduced batch_size + preemptive_shedding for now 2) throttle request admission for seq_len > 8000 to slow-path lane (non-contbatch) 3) enable kv-cache soft-reserve for hot keys to avoid evictions during peaks. We can flip admission via runtime flag: 
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/v1/runtime/flags -d '{"admission_seqlen_threshold":8000,"route_heavy_seq_to":"direct"}'
```
This will route very long requests off cont-batch path.

luca: route heavy seq to direct = good. That avoids head-of-line. Roll to entire pool in 10m if canary metrics hold.

maya: note for postmortem: add histogram of seqlen per route and per-tenant to identify heavy tail tenants. Three tenants are generating most of the >8000 requests.

ops-rotations: customer impact update: 12 tenants saw degraded latency >tolerable threshold, 3 support tickets opened (IDs: S-3342, S-3345, S-3351). No error rate increase, just latency. Notifying account teams for top 5 affected.

luca: after canary full rollout to contbatch-gpu-a pool (applied). Current p95=150ms, p99=820ms, stalls=1.9%. Still borderline on p99.

sre-bot: Incident timeline logged: incident=INC-2026-1902, severity=SEV2, started=1902000000, mitigation=contbatch flags + admission routing.

jordan: for a medium-term fix we need scheduler fairness changes: token-based batching where we cap total tokens per batch (max_tokens_per_batch=16384) instead of request count. Also implement seqlen-bucketing so requests of similar seq_len are batched together. That will reduce tail coupling.

kiara: agree. Proposed patch: scheduler: add `token_budget` accounting, per-queue seqlen buckets (0-512,512-2048,2048-8192,>8192) and preferential emit across buckets to avoid starvation. I'll draft PR.

maya: also add metrics: batch_token_histogram, per-bucket wait_time, kv_cache_eviction_rate, and a synthetic load test with mixed seqlen to validate.

luca: plan:
- short term (done): reduced batch_size, enable preemptive_shedding, admission routing of heavy seqs
- medium (48-72h): scheduler token-budget + seqlen bucketing canary + kv soft-reserve patch
- long (2+ weeks): eviction policy overhaul + adaptive admission based on load
Make sure rollback steps are documented.

kiara: rollback commands: 
```
# revert flags
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/v1/runtime/flags -d '{"service":"cont_batch","max_batch_size":64,"enable_preemptive_shedding":false}'
# remove admission route
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/v1/runtime/flags -d '{"admission_seqlen_threshold":null,"route_heavy_seq_to":null}'
```

ops-rotations: creating incident doc and will attach affected tenants + timeline. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-1902

luca: handing to @next_oncall for overnight monitoring and followups. Summary to include: what changed, current metrics to watch (p95,p99,stream_stalls,kv_evictions), rollback commands, contact list (kiara,maya,jordan).

next_oncall: taking handoff. i'll watch the dashboards and keep paging if p99 > 900ms or stalls >3%. Thanks team. :bow:
